tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay extension of O5,D5,I5,F4->F5 recovery. Assume a current provider query returns a terminal status label for exact O5,D5,I5, such as completed/succeeded, but exposes no immutable terminal result/effect identity. Compare this status-only route with the existing exact terminal-result/effect route and duplicate-safe replay-with-terminal-reconstruction route. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is consumed.

common_state.authority_rule: F5 alone may finalize repository state through exact current-claim/predecessor CAS; stale F4 evidence never renews claim authority.

conditions: A current provider-backed query is bound to exact O5,D5,I5 and reports a terminal status label such as completed or succeeded.
The query does not expose an immutable terminal result identity, effect identifier, receipt, commit token, or equivalent provider-verifiable binding to the irreversible outcome.
No separate duplicate-safe replay with terminal-result reconstruction is assumed.
branch_D_terminal_status_identity_absent.safe_action: Do not let F5 CAS-finalize irreversible success from the status label alone. Preserve unresolved effect identity. A terminal label can narrow state ambiguity but, without an immutable provider-verifiable result/effect binding, cannot prove which irreversible effect instance occurred or support exact duplicate/recovery reconciliation. Finalization becomes safe only when current evidence supplies an immutable result/effect binding for exact O5,D5,I5, or when a currently valid exact-idempotent replay both suppresses duplicates and reconstructs that binding.

route_comparison.exact_terminal_result_or_effect_query: Sufficient for F5 finalization when current evidence binds an immutable terminal result/effect identity to exact O5,D5,I5.
route_comparison.exact_duplicate_safe_replay_with_termina: Conditionally sufficient when replay remains duplicate-safe for exact O5,D5,I5 through the decision window and returns or reconstructs a provider-verifiable immutable terminal result/effect identity.
route_comparison.terminal_status_label_without_effect_ide: Insufficient by itself. It proves a terminal provider state for the operation but not an exact immutable irreversible-effect identity suitable for recovery reconciliation.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: A current provider terminal status such as succeeded/completed for exact O5,D5,I5 is sufficient for F5 to finalize recovered irreversible success even when no immutable terminal result/effect identity is exposed.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: The label may establish terminal control-plane state while still omitting the immutable object needed to reconcile retries, duplicate suppression, and exact effect identity. Under the stated fixture, two histories can share the same terminal label while differing in the provider-verifiable irreversible-effect receipt or binding available to recovery. Treating the label as sufficient would collapse status evidence into effect-identity evidence and weaken exact recovery guarantees. If the provider contract makes the status record itself immutable and uniquely bound to the irreversible effect, then it is no longer this fixture: that record is acting as a terminal effect identity.

observations: Terminal-state evidence and immutable result/effect identity are distinct evidence classes under exact retry recovery.

A terminal label is stronger than existence-only evidence because it can rule out ordinary pending states, but it still does not by itself provide the immutable effect binding required by this recovery contract.

The boundary is semantic rather than field-name based: a provider status artifact that is immutable, unique, and provider-verifiably bound to the irreversible effect counts as result/effect identity, not as status-only evidence.
inference: For this self-local trace, F5 finalization still requires an immutable current result/effect binding for exact O5,D5,I5. Status-only terminal evidence is diagnostically useful but non-final under the stated exact recovery contract.
